name: Warren G. Harding
role: U.S. senator from Ohio (1915-1921) and 29th U.S. president (1921-1923)
summary: Harding was a Republican party man who ran on a return to normalcy, meaning lower taxes, protective tariffs, balanced budgets, less government interference in business and no entanglement in a League of Nations. He supported women's suffrage, arms limitation and disarmament by conference, and restricted immigration, and in 1921 he called for political and educational opportunity for black Americans while rejecting social equality and favouring separation.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Harding submitted treaties that limited naval fleets while preserving standing forces, and as senator voted to expand the Army and authorize a draft.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: Harding signed the Revenue Act of 1921, which revised federal income tax rates and retained the income tax.

arms-reduction.rationale: Harding submitted the signed Washington treaties to the Senate, including the Five-Power Treaty that capped capital-ship tonnage and halted capital-ship construction subject to specified exceptions.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Called for making the alien respect American institutions, magnifying the American viewpoint to those seeking citizenship and Americanizing immigrants.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: At the 1921 unemployment conference Harding opposed relying on Treasury spending to address the downturn.

bound-labor.rationale: Harding’s approval of the end of serfdom appears in a survey of social change. The address does not take up the legal mobility of farmers.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Harding signed the Budget and Accounting Act, establishing an executive budget submitted to Congress within the existing appropriations system.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Held that parties are the governing agencies of representative government and said he would ever have it so.

central-planning.rationale: Asked for an end to government experiments in business and rejected wild experiments with the economic system.

class-collaboration.rationale: During the coal strike Harding convened representatives of the mine operators and the United Mine Workers to negotiate a working agreement.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Harding opposed organizing politics around class antagonism. He did not make a claim about what chiefly drives history in these addresses.

collective-bargaining.rationale: During the coal dispute Harding’s administration sought conferences between mine operators and union representatives to agree on an extension or replacement of their wage agreement.

collective-defense.rationale: Harding voted against ratifying the Versailles treaty without reservations and supported ratification with the Lodge reservations, which withheld a commitment to enforce Article X unless Congress authorized action.

conscription.rationale: Harding voted to adopt the conference report authorizing the wartime military draft in May 1917.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Said the success of popular government rests on the deliberate popular will.

decide-locally.rationale: Harding favored a local role in schooling children and a federal role in educating immigrants. The allocation he proposed for these specific cases does not specify a general rule of local decision-making.

democracy-best.rationale: Called representative popular government the highest expression and surest guaranty of liberty and said democracy is the ideal political state.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: Harding argued that parties channel genuine disagreements into representative government and urged the South to abandon its one-party political alignment.

democratic-peace.rationale: Harding expressed a hope that freedom would end warfare. He did not state that actively spreading democracy produces peace.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Harding opposed Bolshevik propaganda and revolutionary upheaval, but these messages do not address the proposed transitional class dictatorship itself.

direct-action.rationale: Harding opposed strikes in essential services and separately defended constitutional remedies. The labor proposals do not address replacing electoral politics with direct action.

direct-votes.rationale: Harding defended representative party government but did not address direct votes on major laws in the cited speech.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Said racial amalgamation there cannot be and endorsed each race preserving its own racial purity and pride.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Harding credited divine inspiration and called the popular will the basis of successful representative government. Neither claim specifies whether political authority ultimately comes from God.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Harding opposed commercial isolation for the United States. The address does not discuss whether a colonial empire should operate as a closed trading bloc.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Harding opposed the League Covenant as negotiated. His position on that specific covenant does not settle the enforcement powers of the later United Nations.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Said America could be a party to no permanent military alliance.

equal-conscription.rationale: The 1917 draft law Harding voted for subjected men to compulsory military service.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said black citizens should have all the rights of others and fair treatment, but he also held to an inescapable racial difference.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Said equal opportunity had been attained, and that Providence gave men unequal capacities so equal results never follow.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The quota law used country of birth to limit new admissions. That action does not settle what ethnic composition Harding thought the nation as a whole should have.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Harding transferred the naval oil reserves to Interior under his own supervision. The order placed administration of reserves under statutes permitting additional wells and leases, and Interior went on to lease acreage at Teapot Dome.

farm-price-support.rationale: Backed expanded federal farm credit, cooperative marketing and emergency tariffs for agriculture, though denying legislation could cure price swings.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Harding praised the Union soldiers’ call to prevent secession and said preserving the country’s institutions justified their wartime sacrifice.

free-trade.rationale: Harding signed the Fordney–McCumber Tariff, which raised import duties to protect American industry.

generational-constitutional-review.rationale: Harding recommended amendments when backed by considered public opinion. He did not address a scheduled constitutional review for each generation.

gradual-change.rationale: Argued for restoration over revolution, adjustment over agitation and experiment, and said wild experiment would only add confusion while the proven system should be administered efficiently.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Harding signed import controls that limited narcotics to medical and other legitimate purposes and placed their importation under federal control.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Called for less government interference with business and an end to government experiments in business, and presented the existing private system as the base to build on.

military-superiority.rationale: The Washington settlement limited fleet size but permitted the United States a larger capital-ship allowance than several powers and parity with Britain. It does not establish a general demand for superiority over rivals.

nation-first.rationale: Preferred sustainment in triumphant nationality to submergence in internationality and said tranquility at home mattered more than peace abroad, while still favouring conferences.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Harding wanted treaty commitments made in the exercise of national sovereignty. He did not state which law should prevail when an existing international obligation conflicts with the Constitution.

national-mission.rationale: Offered America as an example, but sought no part in directing the destinies of the Old World.

national-rebirth.rationale: Wanted a return to normalcy rather than radical rebirth.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Asked Congress for farm credit, reclamation, federal aid for roads and education and railway regulation.

no-central-bank.rationale: Harding voted to adopt the conference report on H.R. 3673, which revised the Federal Reserve Act and continued the system.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Said contempt for law, even prohibition law that is thought to restrict personal liberty, will ultimately destroy the Republic.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Said government runs through parties and he expected the party in power to take responsibility.

one-party-rule.rationale: Defended government by competing political parties and wished the South not to be solidly of one party.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Believed the party in power should settle policy in conference and then adhere to it, subject to the good of the Republic.

patriotic-education.rationale: Harding called for Americanizing education for immigrants seeking citizenship. The proposal does not extend to a general requirement that schools teach patriotism.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: Harding defended changing the government through constitutional procedures and said attempts to overthrow it by force forfeited the protections owed to lawful dissent.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Said every commitment must be made in the exercise of national sovereignty and refused a super-government.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Pledged to hold fast to the American inheritance and called for magnifying the national viewpoint and the Americanizing of newcomers.

public-ownership.rationale: Called government operation of the railways, the wartime experiment, a supreme folly and said it did not offer the cure; asked for an end to government experiments in business.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: Harding voted to override the veto of the Immigration Act of 1917, which barred immigration from a large designated zone of Asia.

race-social-construct.rationale: Described racial difference as fundamental, eternal and inescapable.

racial-franchise.rationale: Harding voted to table a proposed whites-only suffrage amendment in 1918 and voted for the Nineteenth Amendment without that racial restriction in 1919.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Warned against group and class organizations and denounced demagogues who array group against group, and urged black voters to divide between parties.

racial-pride.rationale: Urged the inculcating of race pride and ambition in the black community and said pride in one's race is the way to natural separation.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Harding signed the Emergency Quota Act, limiting annual admissions from covered countries to three percent of their foreign-born populations in the 1910 census.

religion-illusion.rationale: Harding professed belief in divine inspiration. The address does not discuss whether religion offers illusory comfort for material suffering.

restore-past-order.rationale: Called for restoration, yet said the old order would not return and that the country should go on as well as preserve.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Proposed that labor tribunal rulings be binding in essential public services and that strikes not be timed to paralyze them.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: Harding argued that American grievances should be addressed through constitutional politics and rejected revolutionary overthrow as a remedy in the United States.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Harding authorized specific emergency relief for the Russian famine. One relief decision does not establish a universal duty of wealthy countries to give substantial aid.

right-to-secede.rationale: Harding praised the Civil War settlement for making the Union indissoluble and treated the defeat of secession as a result to preserve.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Harding wanted population and opportunity to be less concentrated in large cities. He did not rank rural and urban life by moral health.

separated-powers.rationale: Pledged to restore cooperation between executive and Congress, disclaiming encroachment on its functions.

small-step-social-reform.rationale: Harding urged postwar reform through adjustment and continuity with inherited American institutions, and rejected revolutionary reconstruction.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Defended the constitutional machinery and its efficient administration, opposing advocates of revolution.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Condemned slackerism and treason in wartime and called for universal service.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Called for respect for law and said the executive should not be enlarged; urged every person to abide by the law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Harding defended a constitutional order that recognized no class in law. The address does not address the claim about which class in fact controls the state.

state-harmful.rationale: Called representative government the highest expression and surest guaranty of liberty and civilization.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Pledged non-involvement in Old World affairs and no entangling alliance.

strong-leader.rationale: Said executive powers were already too large, disavowed any wish to enlarge them and promised no dictation of Congress, preferring cooperation with the legislature.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Harding commuted the sentence of Socialist leader Eugene Debs, imprisoned for an antiwar speech, and in the Senate voted against the 1918 bill expanding penalties for wartime dissent.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Harding put higher protective rates into effect by signing the Fordney–McCumber Tariff.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Harding signed the Revenue Act of 1921, which added graduated surtaxes to the normal income tax and set the top surtax bracket at 50 percent for 1922

territorial-expansion.rationale: Said the United States covets no conquest, has no territorial greed and seeks nothing which is another's.

total-state.rationale: Warned that people expect too much of government, wanted less interference and government out of business.

unions-good.rationale: Harding defended workers’ right to organize on equal terms with employers and to appoint agents to represent them in labor disputes.

universal-morality.rationale: The conference address calls for respecting the participating nations’ rights and aspirations. It does not specify a moral rule that holds across all cultures.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: In the second annual message Harding insisted on obeying prohibition even where people regarded it as an unwarranted restriction of personal liberty.

war-builds-character.rationale: The speeches discuss war’s costs and praise wartime service. They do not state whether war strengthens national character.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.

women-suffrage.rationale: Harding voted for the federal amendment that barred denial of voting rights on account of sex.

notes: This pass checked the annual messages, the Miller Center speech collection, the Senate roll calls and the presidential record. It searched taxation, banking, budgets, trade, labor, constitutional and party government, civil liberties, race, suffrage, immigration, conservation, industrial technology, foreign relief, military commitments, disarmament and means of political change. Birmingham distinguished political and educational opportunity from social equality. National-origin quotas and legally enforced racial segregation are separate questions.
